questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place which had a culture very different to denmark to both try living in such a culture, and also to experince and the learn sociology from a perspective different from what i've allready had during my studies in denmark. For those reasons and for the fact that Seoul offered both rich culture and multiple universities to choose between i went there. It wasnt the most thought through decision, but came from a desire to try something completely different to what i had experienced before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i was not to impressed by the academics at my host institution, but still enjoyed a lot of it and socially it was a great experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I felt like we got the information needed although it was a bit overwhelming at the start to figure out new student platforms and such. We did however get most of the information we needed at orientation and it worked well fromt there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a orientation the first day which helped us get to know campus and the different student platforms. The school also had a buddy programme i did not use myself but i think it was usefull to those that needed help. I feel like the school did what it could to help us the most upon arrival, but still it was a bit much to figure out everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my apartement that i shared with a friend through one of the many facebook-groups offering appartment rental. It was a bit difficult to manage your way around the selection of rentals. but we ended up having a videocall with our landlord which i would also recommend to future exchange students to do. Im not sure how much scam is in facebook groups, but i would still advise to be a bit cautious. An easier option would be to apply to a shared house like simple spaces which i know worked great for a lot of people and was relatively affordable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Seoul is a big city! So i would recommend to use Navermap to see how long transportation from your appartment to campus is as transportation times can be quite a lot. I personally really apreciated the freesom and flexibility of living of campus. so i would definitely reccomend that if you can find your way through the sometimes confusing housing groups.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of steps in process, but if you check mails and give yourself reminders it works out fine.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I cant remember all of it, but i think it was easy enough. if you follow the information you recieve in process. The unisity is also good at replying to your messages if you are ever in doubt of anything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a support email you could contact which was helpfull if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get the classes i initially wanted, so be quick at registration. The signup period extended into the second weak of the semester so there was also the chance to change couses after you allready startet. I changed my courses around quite which was nice that it was available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the steps you recieve with mail as they come and use the add/drop period as their might be a chance to get the couse you want allthough you dont get the spot the same time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I honestly was not that impressed by the level of the courses. so if you want to be challenged academically i would advise taking masters courses if you can.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the teachers were really nice and focused on making the students contribute. the style depended a lot on the couse and the individual teachers. Overall i would say that the teaching reminded me more about the way i was taught in highschool but not always in a bad way

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Modern Histories of Asia and Africa:Past and Present
Political & Economic Development in Korea
Comparative Thought and Culture: Horizons East and West
Sociology of Mental Health
Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Modern Histories of Asia and Africa:Past and Present and Sociology of Mental Health, mostly because i think the teachers were the best and most engaging. Comparative Thought and Culture: Horizons East and West, was also pretty good

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to sign up to a monthly subscription to get your Alien Registration card which cost around 800dkk in total

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: grocery shopping was pretty expensive, as well as events. Going out to eat was pretty cheap however

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot actually. I did not participate in any as i could not find a basketball club at campus, but if you wanna do sports, language exchange or social clubs it is available

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think finding a sport club is a good way to get to know koreans as it can otherwise be a bit challenging

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: i would definetely recommend going on trips to places outside seoul to get a better idea of the country as a whole. Also the museum of contemporary art is one of the best art museums i have ever visited

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not to difficult actually. despite the fact that every sign is in korean i dont think that there were to many cultural mistakes you could make as long as you try to be respectfull

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was a bit hard for me personally, but i would say that taking the chance to speak to people and asking them on coffee during lunchbreaks or something like that could work out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the language barrier, but not much besides that

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the culture around going out to eat, as it was a really social thing and often a great and cheap way to start your night  out

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
pack for all seasons as weather change from 30+ degress to -10 degress during the semester.
make sure you have apps such as navermap and kakaotalk before you go as they are broadly used.
Remember to carry cash as it is a bit unpredictable whether or not you can use you credit card.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: get a climate card in a local convinience store as you are gonna use public transport a lot and it its the cheapest way to get around

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: definitely the other exchange students i met. I think it was quite easy to get to know people at the start as everyone is looking to meet new people. dont be afraid to approach people and ask them to do stuff together

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was having ties and obligations back home. so try to be as open and involved with things in korea as possible

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
